title: Recognising self-care ADLs from a wrist accelerometer: grooming and drinking as ICF performance, and where it breaks

dataset.name: Dataset for ADL Recognition with Wrist-worn Accelerometer (HMP)
dataset.record: single tri-axial wrist accelerometer @ 32 Hz, 14 activities of daily living, 13 subjects; self-care activities include brushing teeth, combing hair, eating meat/soup, drinking from a glass
dataset.citation: Bruno B, Mastrogiovanni F, Sgorbissa A, Vercelli T, Zaccaria R. Analysis of human behavior recognition algorithms based on acceleration data. IEEE ICRA 2013; dataset doi:10.24432/C5CS3C (CC-BY 4.0).

proposition: A clinical scale records THAT a person can groom or eat; a wrist accelerometer can record whether they actually DO it -- the ICF performance qualifier. On real single-wrist accelerometer data, under a strict leave-one-subject-out protocol, the ecosystem's dependency-free HAR pipeline separates self-care from locomotion well (self-care-as-self-care 0.94) and recognises grooming (d520, recall 0.77) and drinking (d560, 0.81) cross-subject -- but eating (d550) is NOT distinguished (recall 0.00): its windows collapse into the other hand-to-face gestures. This is the honest boundary of wrist-only self-care recognition.

claims.statement: self-care windows recognised as SOME self-care activity (leave-one-subject-out)
eating (d550) recall -- NOT distinguished (collapses into other hand-to-face gestures)
subjects (all used as a test fold once)

validation.reference: The dataset's own per-trial activity labels (ground truth), scored with a strict leave-one-subject-out protocol (every subject is a held-out test fold once)
validation.data: REAL -- UCI HMP wrist-worn accelerometer (Bruno et al. 2014), 13 subjects, 32 Hz
validation.note: What reproduces: self-care is separable from locomotion on a real wrist (self-care-as-self-care 0.94), and GROOMING (d520) and DRINKING (d560) are recognised cross-subject well above the 0.20 chance level. What does NOT: EATING (d550) is not distinguished (recall 0.00) -- eating-from-a-plate and hand-to-mouth motions collapse into grooming/drinking, so d550 is honestly only self-care-CATEGORY-level here, not task-level. Stair-climbing (contrast) is also weak (0.26). A dependency-free k-NN on 36 features is deliberately simple; a stronger classifier (PhysioML ROCKET) or a wrist+finger sensor would be needed to split the hand-to-face gestures. Washing, dressing and toileting are not in this dataset.

open_questions.q: Eating collapses into the other hand-to-face self-care gestures under a wrist-only sensor (recall 0.00); whether a richer feature set, a stronger model, or an added finger/utensil sensor separates eating from grooming/drinking -- and whether dressing/toileting are recognisable from the wrist at all -- is open. Documented, not escalated.
